title: Piano solos, fear of wrong chords, and playing in one key
summary: Old-time bands demanded the right chords, some pianists could play only one key, and he contrasts that with today's audiences.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Did you ever play many piano solos in the old days in the band? Did they ever take a solo on the piano or anything?
Well, yeah, I take a solo sometimes. Yeah, I take a solo. I mean, in the old days.
They give you a solo. A long time ago did they do that ever?

Yeah, they give you a solo to play. They give you a solo all the time. You know, take down and give a rest until they come up and go out. Quite naturally, there's a lot of things, you know what I mean? You had to do them that destroyed on you what you could take it or not. Make you play. See, that made you make a musician. That would make you scared to let the public would hear what you're making. If you wasn't playing, you had to play the right stuff. Otherwise, people wouldn't think you're playing. But now you can make anything, but people go for it, you see. That's the different nature of people today. But then time, if you make a false chord, well, you just did look at you and frown, the rest of the musicians, you know. You would feel cheap. They'd make you feel cheap, you know what I mean? When you'd get on, they wouldn't bother with you, nothing like that, at that time. But now the more worse you play, the better they like. So you don't know how to do now. That's right.
You get up there and make nothing and ho, oh, and then that's going to take.
That'll sell. That'll sell. And you play something beautiful, they don't want that. See? That's the trouble.
Yes, that would be kind of difficult to be playing all night long and scared to make a wrong chord or anything and make it a lot harder, I'd imagine, in those days.

Well, yeah, you'd always try, you see, at that time, because you knew they was going to try to, you, it was going to ignore you, you know. So you'd always try to make as closer to them chords as you could, see. Of course, sometime he'd play better than the other fella, like they had a couple of good piano players here then at that time, you know, was playing around here. Well, sometime, like Ray Batiste, well, he could play in one key. You see, lots of them fellas could play in one key. Well, that, them fellas that play in one key would have a bad show, because they couldn't play in no other way but in that C or that C sharp, some playing in F sharp, C sharp and F sharp. Well, then a lot of bands wouldn't play that.
Yeah, they couldn't play in brass and-

Some of them would pick it up in air natural for you. You see what I mean? Well, that would make you sound, you know, you couldn't get in there harder because you know you ain't been playing nothing in that air natural. Quite naturally, they hardly play in them keys now, you know. First you play in some guitar with a guitar, he'll have to pick it up in air natural or something like that. But in these places, these pieces now, you'll have to pick up in any key, see. And so he said, he don't know where he's playing, he said, where he's playing? He said, I don't know. I'm just playing. I said, where you playing? I said, I don't know where to go. He said, I don't know. I said, well, just go ahead on and play. I guess I got to find you. See? Well, that's the way you play now. But them times they tell you, here's right. Oh, you're gone. See? They're gone. That's the way they play then. But now they don't answer nothing. You just pick up where they play. And they don't know, some of them.
